 JUDGMENT The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road accident dated 01.02.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 01.02.2021 at about 12.00 pm., the Petitioner and her minor son were proceeding in a Deo Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA53HB8197 as a pillion rider which was driven by her husband towards Sathegala on the extreme left side on MalavalliMaddur Road slowly and cautiously, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations. While so proceeding, when they reached near Dandinamarammana Temple, Malavalli Town, Mandya, suddenly the rider of TVS Moped bearing Reg.No.KA11EM0226 came from Malavalli side in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life,
without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and suddenly took right turn and dashed against the petitioner's Scooter consequent to which the petitioner,
her husband and her minor son fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Malavalli Govt. Hospital, wherein after first aid treatment, due to severe head injuries, the petitioner was referred to NIMHANS hospital, Bangalore, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient from 01.02.2021 to 03.02.2021.
During the course of treatment she underwent bifrontal craniotomy and elevation of depressed fracture with intradural ACF base repair and exteriorization frontal sinus.

Thereafter for further management petitioner was referred back to Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore, wherein admitted as an inpatient, took treatment from 03.02.2021 to 16.02.2021 underwent surgery and discharged with advise for follow up treatment.

entities.text: Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So far she has spent Rs.1,50,000/ towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the date of accident she was hale and healthy, earning her livelihood as a Tailor, earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
On account of said accidental injuries, the petitioner till today cannot attend to her work, which resulted in loss of earning, earning capacity and she is put to great financial hardship.
The Jurisdictional Malavalli Rural Police have registered a case in their Cr.No.19/2021 and filed chargesheet against the said rider of the offending vehicle p/u/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
The 1 st respondent being the RC owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the TVS Moped bearing Reg.No.KA11EM 0226 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

5. The objections of the Respondent No.2:

sentences.text: This respondent admits the issuance of 5 years of liability policy vide No.0720013118P108202868 in respect of the TVS XL bearing No.KA11EM226.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further submitted that the insured vehicle was said to be driven by a person not in possession of valid and effective DL and the 1st respondent knowingly and willfully entrusted his vehicle to such a person at the time of accident.
The jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the TVS u/Sec.3(1) of MV Act.
Further denied the rash and negligent act of the TVSXL driver.

The accident occurred only by the carelessness on the part of the petitioner's husband who was riding the vehicle bearing No.KA53 HB8197 along with two pillion riders in a Zig Zag manner with high speed and came in the wrong side.
There is delay of 3 days in filing the complaint and this shows that the petitioner has colluded with the police.

This respondent denied the accident,
involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident, age, occupation.

The respondent No.2 contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive,
arbitrary and disproportionate.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by rider of TVS Mope bearing Reg. No.KA11EM0226 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?
3. What order or award?
7. The Petitioner in order to prove her case, has examined herself as PW.1 and has got marked 17 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.13 and P.16 to P.19.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N. - Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center was examined as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents as per Exs.P.14 & P.15.

On the other side, the Respondent No.2 has examined its official Mr.Prashanth N.G.  Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as per Exs.R.1 & R.2.
8.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties.

The counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied upon the decision in MFA No.3297/2019 (MVD) :
Smt.Adilakshmamma & Ors. Vs. Sri. Raju B. & anr.
The counsel for the Petitioner has relied upon the decision in 2020 (2) KCCR 1405 (FB) : New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Bijapur Vs. Smt. Yallavva & anr.

sentences.text: On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 10. Issue No.1:

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the TVS Moped bearing Reg.No.KA11EM0226, the petitioner has examined herself as PW.1 and has got marked 6 documents as per Exs.P.7 to P.11 & P.13.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in her affidavit in lieu of her chief examination.
The Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of the offending TVS Moped in the accident.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner's husband himself.
In the crossexamination of PW.1, she has stated that the Road is wide enough for two vehicles to move around.
The traffic was heavy.
She has stated that in Ex.P.4 her age is mentioned as 57 years and the history is given as pedestrian hit by Car due to some mistake.
But nothing worthwhile showing the absence of negligence on the part of the rider of the TVS Moped is elicited.

More over in Ex.P.11 MLC register extract and Ex.P.12 wound certificate of the petitioner, the history is mentioned as the accident between to Two wheeler and the MLC register at Ex.P.11 is the document at first point of time.
11.

Ex.P.10 MVA report reveals that the vehicle bearing No.KA53HB8197 was damaged to its (i)
Front mudguard, right and left indicators damaged and (ii) Front right side body damaged and the TVS moped bearing No.KA 11EM0226 damaged to its (i) Front handle, right foot rest damaged.
This shows that the TVS Moped hit the Deo Scooter from the front side.
The other documents at Exs.P.7 to 11 & 13 i.e., FIR, FIS, spot mahazar, MVA report, MLC register extract and charge sheet are in accordance with the statement given by the petitioner.
No contrary evidence is led against these documents from the side of respondent No.2.

As such, there are no reasons to discard or disbelieve the version of the Petitioner/PW.1.
12.
As per Ex.P.12/Wound Certificate, the petitioner sustained injuries on 01.02.2021 in a RTA.
This shows that on account of the accident the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

As per Ex.P.10,
the accident was not due to any mechanical defect of either of the vehicles.

Therefore, on overall perusal of Exs.P.7 to 11 & 13 it is clear that the accident occurred on 01.02.2021 and the petitioner sustained injuries as mentioned in Ex.P.12 and the sole reason for the occurrence of the accident was rash and negligent riding by the rider of the TVS Moped bearing No.KA11EM0226.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.12.

As per Ex.P.12, the Petitioner has sustained - (i)
Depressed fracture forehead, right eye swollen, bleeding from nose and (ii) Right leg, upper 1/3rd swelling, Tenderness, deformity which are grievous in nature.

Disability:
16. On perusal of the evidence of PW.2 it is clear that he has assessed the disability of the petitioner.
The injuries suffered by the petitioner have affected her mobility.
17. The petitioner has averred that, at the time of accident she was a Tailor self employed and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
From the evidence of PW.2 it can be seen that the disability being suffered by the petitioner will impact on her daily activities.
However, the total disability of the whole body at 14% estimated by PW.2 cannot be accepted as it appears to be on a higher side.
Therefore, the court deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 10%.

Monthly income:
18.
The Petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, she was a Tailor self employed and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
In support of this she has not produced any documents such as Bank statement, vouchers etc., and also not examined any witness to prove her earnings.

sentences.text: has held that there is a continuous and consistent trend by the Apex Court that the Minimum Wages Act provide for a source by which the notional income of the deceased, who had no valid proof of income could be assessed.
.......The range of the wages between highly skilled and unskilled labour may have to be considered by the Tribunal while assessing the income of the deceased........

However, such guidelines cannot take the place of statutory guidelines and therefore we hold that it would be proper to rely on the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act as a guideline and assess whether the deceased was a skilled or unskilled laborer.

Therefore the notional income of the petitioner can be rounded off to Rs.11,500/ per month.
21. At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 29 years as could be made out from Ex.P.5/Notarized copy Aadhar Card.
She was hale and healthy before the accident.
The accident took place in the year 2021.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

Hospital, Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore and thereafter due to severe head injuries referred to NIMHANS Hospital, Bangalore, wherein took treatment as an inpatient and treated from 01.02.2021 to 03.02.2021, after surgery discharged with advice.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
On perusal of Ex.P.5, as on the date of accident she was 29 years old.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.2,34,600/ (Rs.11,500/ x 12 x 17 x 10%= Rs.2,34,600/) under this head.

sentences.text: The Petitioner was aged about 29 years at the time of accident.
She has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, she is suffering from 10% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout her life.
She will suffer in her mind that she is no more a normal woman.
This will have an adverse effect on the future life of the petitioner.
Because of this she will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND  NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 17 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period she must have spent considerable amount on her food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.2, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implants and the estimation of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/.
In this regard neither the petitioner nor PW.2 has produced any estimation bill about further surgery.

As per the evidence of Pws.1 & 2 and looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

22. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.40,000/

Medical expenses Rs.10,831/

sentences.text: The Respondent No.2 in the written statement has specifically denied the involvement of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA11EM0226 in the accident.
It has contended that, the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself but has not proved the same.
24. The Respondent No.2 has contended that the rider of the TVS Moped did not have a valid DL at the time of accident.
Ex. P.13
the charge sheet filed by the police also shows that the rider was charged u/Secs.3(1) & 181 of the MV Act.
Therefore, it can be held that there is breach of the terms of the contract by the owner/insured and the insurer i.e., the respondent No.2 is not under any liability to indemnify him.

The entire liability of paying the award amount is on the respondent No.1.
25.

The counsel for the petitioner has argued that as per New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva reported in 2020(2) KCCR 1405(FB), the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that the Tribunal may order for pay and recovery when the insurance company successfully establishes that there is breach of any condition recognize u/Sec.149(2).

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva reported in 2020(2) KCCR 1405(FB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This decision is based on the Principles laid down in Pappu Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba - (2018) 3 SCC 2008 and Shamanna Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.,  (2018) 9 SCC 650, wherein the Hob'ble apex court has observed that "mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

entities.text: Pappu Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba - (2018) 3 SCC 2008
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Shamanna Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.,  (2018) 9 SCC 650
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time".
Further the apex court has held that 'the Tribunal can direct the insurance company to pay the award amount to the claimants and inturn recover the same from the owner of the vehicle".

On the other hand the respondent No.2 has relied on the decision of MFA No.3297/2019 (MVD)
between Aadilakshmamma and Ors. Vs. Raju B. and Anr. Dated 13.04.2023 wherien

entities.text: Aadilakshmamma and Ors. Vs. Raju B. and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that when the owner consciously handed over the vehicle to a person who did not possess DL the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover.
In this case, the respondent No.1 is the owner cum driver of the TVS moped.
The insurance company has not proved that he conciously drove the TVS Moped in the absence of DL.

Therefore,
the Tribunal deems it just that the insurance company i.e., Respondent No.2 may be directed to pay the award amount to the petitioner and later recover the same from the respondent No.1 i.e., the owner/driver of the vehicle.
The petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.9,00,000/ but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.3,57,000/ with interest @6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to allowed.
Accordingly, issue No.2 held in the Affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues this court proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,57,000/ (Rupees Three Lakhs Fifty Seven Thousand only) from the Respondent No.1 along with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.

The 1 st respondent being the RC owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the TVS Moped bearing Reg.No.KA11EM 0226 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed exparte.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further submitted that the insured vehicle was said to be driven by a person not in possession of valid and effective DL and the 1st respondent knowingly and willfully entrusted his vehicle to such a person at the time of accident.
The jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the TVS u/Sec.3(1) of MV Act.
Further denied the rash and negligent act of the TVSXL driver.
The accident occurred only by the carelessness on the part of the petitioner's husband who was riding the vehicle bearing No.KA53 HB8197 along with two pillion riders in a Zig Zag manner with high speed and came in the wrong side.
This respondent denied the accident,
involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident, age, occupation.
The respondent No.2 contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive,
arbitrary and disproportionate.
